newsitem.title: USA: U.S. administration sees trade deficit stabilizing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. administration sees trade deficit stabilizing.

text.p: The Clinton administration said on Thursday it expects the U.S. trade and current account deficits to stabilize around current levels through the 1998 fiscal year.

In its budget proposal, the administration projected a trade deficit for the fiscal year that starts on October 1 of between $170 billion and $210 billion and a current account deficit of $140 billion to $180 billion.
In the 1996 fiscal year, which ended last September 30, the merchandise trade deficit was $181 billion and the current account shortfall was $154 billion.
